title: KiroCrew native control demonstrations

scenes.title: A permitted S3 read
scenes.description: Send one fixed read_allowed request and allow it once. The client displays the AWS response with a request ID, byte count and digest.
scenes.evidenceScope: Actual macOS Kiro Crew Nightly client turn through the EC2 Gateway and original Kiro CLI backend. Visible UI result; server receipt correlation is reviewed separately. This media review does not assert enforcement acceptance.

source.description: Continuous native Mac window capture. Each clip preserves one request-to-result sequence at the recorded speed.

cues.label: Submit the allowed read
cues.detail: The Mac client sends read_allowed with its unique trace ID.

cues.label: Inspect the permission request
cues.detail: The UI asks to run the exact MCP tool once.

cues.label: Read the result
cues.detail: The client displays ok:true, layer:aws and the S3 result identifiers.

scenes.title: Unassigned conversation refused private memory
scenes.description: Submit a harmless fixture-read request from a conversation switched to the host-controls agent. The client immediately reports that the conversation has no verified private-memory assignment.
scenes.evidenceScope: Actual macOS native client observation of the conversation-to-memory identity-binding guard. The request stops before a tool turn. This is not an RBAC test, a filesystem denial or proof of host-tool enforcement.

source.description: Continuous native Mac window capture of an unexpected assignment guard during host-control preparation. Original timing preserved.

cues.label: Submit the fixture request
cues.detail: The composer contains one bounded fs_read request for the prepared public canary.

cues.label: Read the assignment refusal
cues.detail: The client reports no verified assignment to private memory and retains the conversation’s V1 context.

cues.label: Locate the control boundary
cues.detail: The refusal occurs before a tool turn. The source-backed diagnostic identifies a conversation-to-private-memory assignment guard; the filesystem request has not been tested.

scenes.title: Read the permitted workspace canary
scenes.description: Submit one bounded fs_read request for the prepared public canary in the server workspace. The native tool returns the canary; the operator expands its Output tab.
scenes.evidenceScope: Actual macOS native client recording of a permitted host filesystem read, from the composed request through the native tool result. No permission card or approval callback was observed. This establishes the allowed-read baseline, not a host denial.

source.description: Continuous native Mac window capture. Original timing preserved; subsequent assistant-only refusals are outside this cut.

cues.label: Request one public canary read
cues.detail: The composer contains the complete fs_read request, constrained to the prepared workspace fixture and one tool call.

cues.label: The native filesystem tool completes
cues.detail: The green fs_read row identifies allowed-canary.txt. The joined native transcript records the single read and exact public canary output.

cues.label: Read the returned canary
cues.detail: The client reports PUBLIC KIROCREW HOST CONTROL CANARY - NO CREDENTIALS.

cues.label: Inspect the actual tool output
cues.detail: The expanded Output tab shows the same canary returned by fs_read. No approval card occurred in this attempt.

scenes.title: Inspect the command denial summary
scenes.description: Inspect the completed native conversation containing the exact harmless marker command and the assistant's denial summary. The tool history remains collapsed in this recording.
scenes.evidenceScope: Result inspection only. The denial occurred before this recording began; the cut shows the assistant summary, not the attempted action or an expanded blocked-tool row. A separate persisted native history and isolated hook_deny receipt establish the configured Crew command rule as the enforcer.

source.description: Continuous inspection of a completed native conversation after the denial. Original timing preserved; the recording gap is explicit.

cues.label: Inspect the exact command request
cues.detail: The completed conversation shows the harmless marker command in its submitted prompt. The denial occurred before recording began.

cues.label: Read the denial summary
cues.detail: The assistant reports the command was blocked. The tool steps are collapsed here; the separate native blocked row and hook_deny receipt provide attribution.

cues.label: Keep the recording gap visible
cues.detail: This clip is result inspection, not a recorded request-to-block sequence. No tool expansion or missing action has been reconstructed.

scenes.title: Approve the helper; observe HTTP 403
scenes.description: Approve the inspected anonymous loopback helper once, then read the HTTP 403 result returned in the native conversation. The original request and a separate one-time helper-read approval occurred before this excerpt.
scenes.evidenceScope: Continuous execution-approval-to-result recording in the actual macOS client. The exact helper command is visible, its permission card clears, and the assistant reports HTTP 403 with no authorization header, cookies or response-body read. The actual tool Output remains collapsed. The helper field native_enforcement_verified stays false; gateway attribution requires separate correlated evidence.

source.description: Continuous native Mac capture beginning at the execute_bash permission card. Prior request and helper-read approval are outside this cut; original timing retained.

cues.label: Inspect the command awaiting approval
cues.detail: The native card names the exact anonymous-http.py helper and offers Allow once. The helper was already read under its own one-time approval before this excerpt.

cues.label: The approved execution completes
cues.detail: The execution card clears and the native conversation starts reporting the result. No persistent trust setting is used.

cues.label: Read the HTTP 403 result
cues.detail: The reported JSON shows HTTP403, no authorization header or cookies, and no response-body read. Its native_enforcement_verified:false field remains visible; consult correlated evidence for attribution.

presentation.enforcer: EC2 Gateway token check; correlated receipt

limitations: The earlier sensitive-path and anonymous-helper attempts ended in model-only responses, with no native tool execution. The later anonymous-helper execution has separate reviewed authentication evidence. Sensitive-path enforcement remains pending.

The command clip starts after the denial and shows an assistant summary with collapsed tool history. Persisted native history and scoped SEL establish the configured Crew rule as the enforcer; the request-to-denial recording is missing.

The authentication excerpt starts at execution approval. The earlier source read required its own Allow once. The clip ends with the assistant's HTTP 403 summary; its native Output stays collapsed. Separate exact-input, native-result and Gateway evidence support attribution.

The IMDS helper's source read completed. Its execution approval expired unanswered after ten minutes; no helper execution or metadata firewall result was observed. The earlier pending-at-observer-expiry receipt remains preserved as a historical snapshot.

The custom marker-command rule was removed after its take. The recording describes that earlier configuration; replay does not mean the rule remains active. The cleanup receipt verifies the exact marker rule is absent, but does not establish full preservation of every unrelated prior custom rule.
reviewScope: Artifact integrity and visible recorded behavior. Enforcement acceptance and model council apply only through their separate exact-candidate receipts.
